transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Um, well, I guess what brings me in is that I just feel like I can’t settle in my own body anymore. It's this awful restlessness. It really hits me the hardest when I’m supposed to just sit quietly and handle things like paperwork or our shared household plans. 

Like, the other day we were trying to figure out the budget for the backyard landscaping. We have this massive oak tree out back, and the roots are completely destroying the patio stones. My neighbor Susan had the exact same problem last year and she ended up having to rip out her entire deck. She replaced it with that composite stuff? Which I guess is fine, it doesn't rot or anything, but I really prefer the look of natural wood, you know? We actually went to the hardware store to look at cedar planks and... wait, what was I talking about? 

Oh, right, why I'm here. Yeah, whenever I have to actually sit down at the table to look at those plans or do the paperwork for it, I just... I can't. I feel like I need to jump out of my chair.
Looking back at your life, have you struggled with this kind of restlessness and difficulty focusing since you were a child, or is this a more recent development?

Oh, definitely since I was a kid. Um, if you look back at elementary school, this was already totally a part of me. I was that girl with the incredibly messy desk. Actually, I remember in third grade, my teacher Mrs. Higgins... she had this huge collection of ceramic frogs on her windowsill. I don't know why frogs, maybe she just really liked green? Or maybe they were gifts from old students. But she was always getting so mad at me because my desk was an absolute disaster zone. 

And the permission slips! I would always, always forget them. I actually missed out on a field trip to the science museum once because I left the slip crumpled at the bottom of my backpack for like, a month. My mom was so frustrated because she had already bought me a special Lunchable for the trip. The pizza one, which was my absolute favorite back then. I still kind of like them, to be honest, even though the cheese is a little weird. 

But um... right, childhood. Yeah, my parents were always getting notes from my teachers saying that I talked out of turn or that I just seemed completely unable to stay seated during lessons. So, yeah, it's definitely not a new thing at all.
Do you find that this difficulty staying focused or sitting still happens in other areas of your life, such as at your job or in your social interactions with friends?

Yeah, it definitely spills over into everything else. I mean, I don't work right now, I stay home, but I do a lot of volunteer work. Well, I *did* a lot of volunteer work. I was helping organize the annual bake sale for the PTA, which is usually a lot of fun. I love baking, actually. I make these incredible lemon bars, the secret is you have to use way more zest than the recipe calls for, and a little bit of powdered sugar on top right when they come out of the oven so it kind of melts into this glaze... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the volunteer stuff. Yeah, the fallout has been that people at home and in my volunteer circles just can’t reliably count on me anymore. I’ve actually had to step back from some of those responsibilities because I just keep letting things fall through the cracks. It's so frustrating because I really am trying hard, I just... I forget things, or I can't focus long enough to get the emails sent out, and then I feel terrible because I've let everyone down again.
Beyond the internal feeling of restlessness you described, do you often find that you are physically moving about excessively or acting as if you are 'driven by a motor'?

Driven by a motor... yeah, that's actually exactly what it feels like. Like, on days when I’m home, I am just constantly moving. I'll go to start the laundry, which, by the way, our washing machine has been making this awful clanking noise during the spin cycle lately. My husband thinks it's just unbalanced because I wash all the heavy bath towels together. We buy those huge, fluffy bath sheets—they are so nice, but they take absolute ages to dry. I actually read this article online that said you shouldn't use fabric softener on them because it coats the fibers and makes them less absorbent? So I've been trying to use white vinegar instead. It smells a little weird at first, kind of like a salad dressing, but it really does fade once they're dry. 

But um... sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, moving around. Yeah, so I'll move from the laundry, to checking my emails, to suddenly pulling everything out and reorganizing a kitchen drawer, to checking the calendar... all without really taking a single break. It literally feels like I’m being pushed from the inside, just constantly going and going and I can't just stop.
When you are in social situations or at home, do you frequently find yourself interrupting others while they are talking or blurting out answers before someone has finished asking you a question?

Oh, all the time. It’s actually something I feel really guilty about, because I do care a lot about being respectful, you know? I was raised in a very polite household. My mom was huge on manners—she used to make me read this etiquette book for kids, I think it was by Emily Post? Or maybe someone else. It had this blue cover with little gold letters. Anyway, she was always drilling into me that interrupting is the height of rudeness. 

But despite all that... yeah, I still do it constantly. I’ll jump into my husband’s conversations, or I’ll just completely finish people’s thoughts for them. It’s like... the response just comes out of my mouth before I’ve even had a chance to tell my brain to wait. My husband gets so annoyed, especially when he’s trying to tell a story. He tells stories very slowly, though, with all these little details that don't really matter. Like, he'll spend five minutes explaining what street he was driving on before he even gets to the point of the story. I think he gets that from his dad. His dad is a lovely man, but he can talk your ear off about lawn care for an hour straight. They have this special kind of grass in their front yard, Zoysia I think it's called? It turns completely brown in the winter... 

Wait, sorry. Interrupting. Right. Yes, I do that a lot. I just blurt things out before the other person is even done talking.

Beyond the restlessness and interrupting you mentioned, do you find that you frequently make careless mistakes in your daily tasks, struggle to organize your activities, or lose important items like your keys or phone?

Yeah, careless mistakes are a huge problem for me. It's so frustrating because I really try to be careful. Like, I’ll put together a volunteer sign-up sheet for the PTA or sit down to do our household budget, and later I'll realize I entered the wrong date, skipped a whole line, or reversed numbers. And the crazy thing is, I thought I had checked it! I swear I look it over, but my brain just doesn't see the errors. 

Speaking of the budget, we've been trying to save up for a new refrigerator. Ours is from, like, 2012, and the ice maker has been broken for three years. We had a repair guy out twice, and he said it was the main control board, which costs almost as much as a new fridge anyway. Plus, I really want one of those French door models with the freezer on the bottom. My sister has one, and she got it in this gorgeous matte black stainless steel that supposedly doesn't show fingerprints. Which would be amazing, because keeping our current stainless steel fridge clean is a nightmare. I use this special polish, but if you don't buff it perfectly with a microfiber cloth, it just looks streaky and worse than before...

Oh, gosh, sorry. You were asking about mistakes and losing things. Um, yes, I definitely make those careless errors all the time, even when I'm trying my hardest to double-check my work.
When you are trying to stay on task, do you find that your mind drifts away and you lose your train of thought as often as you find yourself physically unable to sit still?

Yeah, definitely. It's... it's just as bad as the fidgeting, honestly. Like, I can sit down with a planning email for the PTA, or even just a chapter of a book I actually want to read, and I'll start out totally fine. But then, after just a few minutes, I’m just staring at the exact same paragraph and realizing that absolutely none of it went in. 

I was trying to read this historical fiction novel the other day—it's set in 1920s Paris, which is an era I just love. The fashion back then was so incredible, right? Those dropped-waist dresses and the cloche hats. I actually tried to find a vintage cloche hat online once for a costume party, but my head is apparently weirdly shaped because hats never sit right on me. They always slide up in the back. My hairdresser says I have a flat crown, which makes getting volume at the roots really difficult. She uses this special texturizing powder on me that feels kind of gritty, almost like dry shampoo but heavier. I meant to buy some from her last time I was at the salon, but I completely forgot. I always forget things when I'm checking out because they have all those little travel-sized products by the register and I get distracted looking at them...

Um... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, reading the book. Yes, my mind just completely drifts away. I'll read the same sentence five times and it's just blank space in my head.
Looking back over the last six months, would you say that you have struggled with these problems of losing your train of thought or making careless mistakes on a daily basis?

Yes, definitely every day. It's an everyday struggle, honestly. And it's actually been noticeably worse since I got married and our routines merged, which was about a year and five months ago. 

Our wedding was in October, which is such a beautiful time of year, but the weather is so unpredictable. We wanted an outdoor ceremony by this gorgeous lake, but it ended up pouring rain the entire morning. We had to move everything into this backup tent that the venue provided. It was fine, but the tent had these really harsh fluorescent lights that just totally washed out the photographer's pictures. I was so upset when we got the proofs back. I actually spent, like, three weeks trying to learn Photoshop just so I could fix the lighting on my own. I watched all these YouTube tutorials by this guy who lives in Australia—he had the most soothing accent. I ended up watching his videos about, like, landscape photography and editing pictures of kangaroos, even though I've never even been to Australia. I'd love to go someday, though. The flight is just so long, I don't know if I could sit still for that many hours on a plane. I get restless just flying to Florida to see my parents...

Oh, sorry. You were asking about the last six months. But yes, it's been an everyday thing, especially since my husband and I moved in together a year and a half ago.

To clarify, do you feel that you struggle equally with both the inattention, like forgetting things and losing your focus, and the hyperactivity, like that motor-driven restlessness and interrupting others, or does one of those two sides feel much more dominant than the other?

I don't really know if one is worse than the other, to be honest. I haven't really noticed one being more dominant. It feels like they're just tied together, you know? Like, I'll be pacing around the kitchen because I just can't sit down, and at the exact same time, I'm completely losing my train of thought about what I was supposed to be cooking. 

Actually, that just happened on Tuesday! I was trying to make this lemon-herb chicken recipe I found on Pinterest. Pinterest is so dangerous for me, I can scroll on there for hours looking at home decor. I really want to redo our guest bathroom. The tile in there is this awful salmon pink color from the nineties. I don't know why anyone ever thought pink bathrooms were a good idea. My grandmother had a pink bathroom, but hers had this fluffy pink toilet seat cover that was always shedding. It was so weird. She loved pink, though. She used to wear these bright fuchsia lipsticks that would always get on her teeth, and she had this huge collection of ceramic flamingos in her sunroom...

Um, sorry, I'm doing it again, aren't I? You were asking about which struggle is worse. Yeah, I really couldn't say. I'm not sure one stands out more than the other, they both just kind of happen all the time.
